newsitem.title: INDIA: India eases foreign investment approval rules.
newsitem.headline: India eases foreign investment approval rules.

text.p: The Indian Industry Ministry liberalised conditions under which foreign investors are granted approval to hold 51 percent in companies in 35 specified industries.

Earlier, companies that required approval from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to invest in these industries could not invest more than an amount they would spend on import of capital goods needed for a project.
The condition has now been abolished, the ministry said in a statement.

In the case of foreign links involving transfer of technology, an existing ceiling of 10 million rupees ($279,000) on payment of fees for technology has been raised to US $2.0 million, the statement said.
